body:
Approved implementation plan (auto-approved gate, epic #99 autonomous run)

Design: the site-policy gate fails closed on every path. New envelope `{ok:false, error:'site policy check failed', reason, message, [tabId]}` with isError:true (distinct from 'site blocked by policy'; no domain/policySource/auto-close; nothing recorded in the event log). Reason codes: policy_error (any exception in the gate or a chain step), extension_disconnected (checkpoint B while the extension is disconnected; same message text as before, now a result envelope instead of JSON-RPC -32000), tab_url_unavailable (get_tabs error/timeout, tab not found, non-string URL), invalid_tab_id (missing or non-integer tab_id on any tab-scoped tool — strings like "7" are rejected, no coercion), invalid_url (non-string url on browser_create_tab; undefined/null/'' still pass to the extension's own "URL is required"). Checkpoint A keeps working while disconnected (it launches Chrome). A found tab with url '' (pending navigation) evaluates to default allow with no event. `_resolveTabUrl` becomes a wrapper over a strict resolver so the formatter gate keeps its lenient behavior. Chain steps: a thrown check becomes that step's envelope and later steps still run.

Sub-tasks:
- [sub-task 1] Tests first in test/site-policy-events-gate.test.js (12 cases; expected red until impl) (standard)
- [sub-task 2] Implement in src/mcp-handler.js (complex) — after 1
- [sub-task 3] CHANGELOG Fixed entry (light)
- [sub-task 4] Verification: suite, grep for "failing open", booted-daemon smoke without the extension (standard) — last

Out of scope: workflow primitives bypassing the gate (#114); the pending-navigation time-of-check gap (#114); #101.
